title: Adaptive Optimization Method for Privacy-Preserving Asynchronous Federated Learning Based on Compression and Event-Triggered Communication

pse.problem: Inefficiencies in asynchronous federated learning due to high delay from low-quality participating nodes and excessive communication cost.
pse.solution_function: The proposed method performs adaptive optimization for privacy-preserving asynchronous federal learning by implementing compression and event-triggered communication. It aims to reduce the delay caused by low-quality nodes and decrease communication overhead.
pse.solution_structure: The system comprises participating nodes, a central server, and a compression module. The participating nodes perform local iterations on the model, apply privacy protection through noise addition, and send compressed updates to the server using event-triggered communication.
pse.solution_implementation: Upon receiving a trigger event, a node compresses its updated model using techniques such as quantization or pruning. The compressed update is then sent to the server when certain conditions are met (e.g., accumulated compression threshold). Upon aggregating updates from multiple nodes, the server updates the global model.
pse.effect: The proposed method reduces delay by only requiring high-quality nodes to transmit their updates and decreases communication cost through compression. This results in improved efficiency and precision of the global model updating.
